questionText: Which of the following statements about threads is/are TRUE?
options: Threads can only be implemented in kernel space
Each thread has its own file descriptor table for open files
All the threads belonging to a process share a common stack
Threads belonging to a process are by default not protected from each other
explanation:
Analysis of each statement:

(A) Incorrect: Threads can be implemented at both the user level (User-Level Threads) and kernel level (Kernel-Level Threads), as well as hybrid models.

(B) Incorrect: Open file descriptors are process-wide resources shared among all threads of that process, rather than maintained separately per thread.

(C) Incorrect: Each thread must have its own separate stack to maintain its execution history, local variables, and function call frames.

(D) Correct: Threads belonging to the same process share the same address space. Therefore, there is no built-in memory protection mechanism between threads within the same process.
